name: Variance / Volatility Swap Replication (Log-Contract Strip)
summary: Replicate a variance swap by holding a strip of out-of-the-money puts and calls across every listed strike, each weighted by 1/K-squared, delta-hedged daily - the standard desk method for trading pure realized-versus-implied variance.

legs.strike_rule: every listed OTM put from the lowest liquid strike up to spot, contracts proportional to (delta-K) / K-squared, normalized so the cheapest strike gets 1 contract
every listed OTM call from spot up to the highest liquid strike, same 1/K-squared weighting
delta hedge: short (or long) shares each day equal to minus the strip's aggregate delta, rebalanced at the close
legs.dte_rule: held and rebalanced daily to expiry

max_profit: Realized variance minus implied variance, times the strip's vega notional - unbounded, and convex in a crash
max_loss: The full strip debit if realized variance is below implied for the whole life; bounded, because every option leg is long
breakevens: Realized volatility over the life equal to the strip's implied volatility, adjusted for hedging slippage

greeks.delta: hedged to zero daily - the hedge P/L IS the trade
greeks.gamma: positive and, by construction, constant in dollar terms across spot levels
greeks.theta: negative every day the underlying does not move
greeks.vega: positive and approximately constant in spot - the defining property of the log contract

when_to_use: When implied variance is rich or cheap relative to a forecast of realized variance and the goal is exposure to variance itself rather than to a direction or a single strike. It is the only structure in the bank whose payoff is a statistic rather than a price.
entry_rules: SCOPE NOTE: this structure requires 20-60 legs and therefore sits outside the bank's four-leg design cap. It is documented for completeness and must be modeled before it is ever submitted.
Long-only version only. The short-variance version (selling the strip) is a naked short across every strike and is BLOCKED - it would require level 4 and would carry unbounded loss in a crash.
SPY or QQQ only; the strip must span at least +/-15% around spot with every strike quoted OI >= 250.

Weight each strike by delta-K / K-squared, then round to whole contracts and re-verify that the rounded strip's vega profile is flat in spot to within 15% - if it is not, widen the strike increment rather than accepting a lumpy strip.
Total debit <= 5% of equity. On $50k that buys a very small variance notional; report the implied variance notional explicitly so the position is not mistaken for a large one.
Daily delta-hedge capability is mandatory. Without the hedge this is not a variance trade, it is an expensive long strangle.
Entry only when 30-day implied variance is below the 25th percentile of the 2-year realized-variance distribution (for the long side).
management_rules: Rebalance the share hedge every day at 15:45 ET to the strip's aggregate delta; log the hedge P/L separately, because it is the realized-variance accrual.
Do not adjust individual strikes. The replication is static by design; touching strikes destroys the flat-vega property.
Take profit when cumulative hedge P/L plus mark-to-market reaches 50% of the debit, or when implied variance rises above its 75th percentile.
Cut the position if two consecutive weeks of realized variance come in below 60% of implied - the forecast was wrong and theta will finish the job.
Never roll the strip; close it and rebuild at the new expiry if the view persists.
exit_rules: Close every option leg at least 3 trading days before expiration - a strip of 20-60 legs cannot be unwound in the final session, and any ITM long leg would auto-exercise into shares.
Flatten the share hedge in the same session the strip is closed, not before and not after.
Never exercise a leg; always sell it.
If any strike becomes unquotable for a full session, close the whole strip - a strip with a hole no longer replicates anything.
assignment_risk: No short legs, therefore no assignment risk. The real operational risk is auto-exercise of several ITM long legs at once, which the three-day close rule prevents, and the share hedge itself, which must be flattened in step with the options.
buying_power: The strip's debit plus margin on the share hedge (which can be short shares, requiring a borrow).
liquidity_needs: Extreme: dozens of strikes in one expiry, all closeable. SPY is the only realistic candidate on this account.
common_mistakes: Skipping the daily hedge and calling a strangle a variance swap; weighting by 1/K instead of 1/K-squared; trying to sell the strip; ignoring that the far wings dominate the weighting and are the least liquid part of the chain.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - variance is measured over the life of the strip.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
